summary: Non-custodial DeFi lending protocol spanning multiple generations and networks. Aave remained operational through a November 2022 CRV bad-debt event and a November 2023 precautionary security pause, and launched Aave V4 on Ethereum and Avalanche in 2026.
what_happened: On 2022-11-22, a large CRV short position on Aave V2 Ethereum was liquidated and left approximately USD 1.7 million of protocol bad debt, later repaid through a DAO treasury process. On 2023-11-04, a vulnerability reported through Aave's security process led the Guardian to pause or freeze affected V2 and V3 pools and assets as a precaution. The affected markets were progressively restored and all V2/V3 pools were operating normally again by 2023-11-16. Aave continued expanding and launched V4 on Ethereum in March 2026 and Avalanche in July 2026.
uncertainty_notes: The 2022 CRV event created protocol bad debt but is not treated as a universal customer-loss amount. The 2023 security response was precautionary and temporary; no protocol-wide customer loss is inferred from the pause itself.
notes: DeFi backfill record. Historically significant incidents are modeled separately while current platform status remains active.
